title: Cut the ball: do the two balls split at a right angle? No spin: 90 degrees. Rolling: 63.7 degrees
description:
Cut the ball: do the two balls split at a right angle? Two cue balls hit a ball at rest half on (the cue ball's centre aimed at the object ball's edge, a 30 degree cut) at 2 m/s, seen from above one panel above the other. The top cue ball arrives sliding with no spin: a stun shot, struck with the little backspin (45.0 rad/s, launched at 2.51 m/s 59.3 cm behind the hit point) that the cloth wears off exactly at the hit. The bottom cue ball arrives rolling (spin v / R = 69.9 rad/s). Equal masses, a solid sphere (I = 2/5 m R^2, radius 28.6 mm), an instantaneous elastic hit with no friction between the balls, so the object ball takes the velocity component along the line of centres (v cos 30 = 1.732 m/s, 30 degrees off the cue line) and the cue ball keeps the perpendicular component (v sin 30 = 1.000 m/s along the tangent line, 60 degrees off its line the other way) and whatever spin it had. The cloth acts on any slipping contact with sliding friction mu = 0.2 (g = 9.80665 m/s^2), no rolling resistance: the slip keeps a fixed direction while it shrinks at 7/2 mu g, so every sliding phase is a constant-acceleration piece. Each panel is integrated as exact pieces between the events (a slip closing, the hit) and checked against the closed forms. Shown at 1/8 speed, one shot every 7 s, 6 shots in 42 s; deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- at the hit both cue balls arrive at 2.0000 m/s with their centres 57.200 mm apart on a line of centres 30.00 degrees off the cue line, the top one with no spin (surface slip 0.0e+00 m/s) and the bottom one rolling at 69.930 rad/s; right after: the object ball 1.7321 m/s at 30.00 degrees, the cue balls 1.0000 m/s at 60.00 degrees the other way, 90.00 degrees apart in both panels; momentum (2.0000, 0.0000) = (2.0000, 0.0000) and energy 2.0000 = 2.0000 per unit mass across the hit
- no spin: the cloth only slows the cue ball along the tangent line (it leaves the line by at most 1e-13 mm); it rolls again at 0.7143 m/s, 5/7 of 1.0000, after 0.1457 s and 12.49 cm of slip (closed forms 0.7143 m/s, 0.1457 s, 12.49 cm, matched within 1e-14); its path and the object ball's path meet at 90.00 degrees
- rolling: right after the hit the slip at the contact is 1.7321 m/s at 150 degrees, one fixed direction, so the cloth's push points one way and the path is a parabola; the cue ball settles at 1.1157 m/s, 33.67 degrees off its old line, after 0.2523 s and 26.23 cm of curve (25.99 cm as the crow flies) (closed form v_final = 5/7 v_after + 2/7 v0: 1.1157 m/s at 33.67 degrees, 0.2523 s, matched within 1e-15); the kept spin bends it 26.33 degrees back from the tangent line; its spin turns from 69.930 rad/s along the old line to 39.012 rad/s along the new one; the two paths meet at 63.67 degrees (30 + 33.67)
- the object ball, both panels: leaves sliding at 1.7321 m/s with no spin and rolls at 1.2372 m/s (5/7) after 0.2523 s and 37.46 cm, its direction unchanged; in the rolling panel it settles at the same instant as the cue ball
- the 30 degree rule (same speed, other cuts, rolling cue ball): three-quarter ball (14.48 degree cut) settles 27.63 degrees off its line at 0.7457 m/s after 16.6 cm, paths 42.10 degrees apart; half ball 33.67 degrees, paths 63.67 apart; quarter ball (48.59 degree cut) 27.27 degrees at 1.5469 m/s after 29.2 cm, paths 75.86 apart; with no spin every cut splits at 90.00
- the angles do not depend on the speed, only the slip distances do: at 1 m/s the no-spin cue ball slips 3.1 cm and the rolling one curves 6.6 cm (90.00 and 63.67 degrees); at 3 m/s 28.1 and 59.0 cm (the same angles); the object ball settles after 9.4, 37.5 and 84.3 cm at 1, 2 and 3 m/s

Why: the hit only passes on the part of the cue ball's motion that points along the line between the two centres. What is left points along the tangent line, at a right angle to the object ball's path, and that is the direction the cue ball leaves in. A ball with no spin has nothing else: the cloth can only slow it along that line, so it keeps the right angle. A rolling ball also keeps its spin, which still points along its old line. The cloth grabs that spinning surface and pushes the ball back toward where it was going, until the speed and the spin agree again and the ball rolls. The push always comes from the contact point, so the final direction is a fixed mix, five parts the tangent-line motion to two parts the old rolling motion, whatever the cloth: the friction only sets how far the curve takes. For a half-ball hit that mix ends 33.7 degrees off the old line, and for anything between a quarter-ball and a three-quarter-ball hit it ends near 30 degrees, the rule of thumb players use to guess where a rolling cue ball goes.

Rerun sims/cutshot/cutshot.py with projects/cutshot/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
